key_insight: A hybrid pipeline uses large language models to elicit and codify diverse expert and stakeholder preferences, then feeds those structured preferences into constrained optimization to prioritize health-post upgrades that maximize population coverage in Ethiopia.
problem_solved: How to prioritize a limited set of health-post upgrades so that scarce resources yield maximal and equitable population coverage while explicitly incorporating heterogeneous expert judgments and stakeholder values.
method: Use LLMs as structured elicitation tools to translate qualitative expert knowledge and stakeholder preferences into formal constraints, weights, and scenario specifications.
Integrate the LLM-derived preference models with an optimization engine (facility-location / integer programming) that maximizes population coverage under capacity, budget, and equity constraints.
Iterate with human-in-the-loop validation (public health institute & ministry stakeholders) and scenario analysis to produce implementable, transparent upgrade plans.
impact: Demonstrates a practical pattern for combining generative LMs with classical optimization to make domain knowledge machine-actionable, improving transparency and stakeholder alignment in high-stakes planning applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: expert interviews → LLM preference extraction → formalized objectives/constraints → optimization → upgrade plan
Choropleth map of Ethiopia: current vs. proposed health-post coverage highlighting coverage gains and underserved regions
Bar or line chart: coverage percentage vs. number of upgrades under different stakeholder-weight scenarios
Trade-off radar or stacked bar: showing how different stakeholder preferences shift priority outcomes (e.g., equity, coverage, cost)
paper_title: Health Facility Location in Ethiopia: Leveraging LLMs to Integrate Expert Knowledge into Algorithmic Planning
paper_authors: Yohai Trabelsi, Guojun Xiong, Fentabil Getnet, Stéphane Verguet, Milind Tambe
